name: code-block
purpose: Read-only code viewer for docs, API examples, and configuration previews. Supports four Figma-documented layouts that share one monolithic shell: 1. **Language switcher** ([4567:33761](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-33761)) — tabbed snippets with a sliding pill, optional filename bar, syntax highlighting, and copy. 2. **Show filename** ([4567:30198](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-30198)) — single snippet with a raised filename bar (language icon + name), no tabs. 3. **Diff** ([4567:29012](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-29012)) — per-line added/removed markers (`+`/`-`), semantic row backgrounds, and a 2 px leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. 4. **Highlighted line** ([4567:31473](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-31473)) — one active line with info background and leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. Regions render conditionally from tab data — the consumer does not pick a separate `kind`. Tab header appears when `tabs.length > 1`. Filename bar appears when the active tab sets `fileName`. Diff and highlight decorations come from `lineChanges` and `highlightedLine` on the active tab. **Syntax highlighting** is driven by the active tab's `language` and resolves to one of these tokenisers, all of which emit the same seven token types (`keyword`, `string`, `function`, `type`, `punctuation`, `identifier`, `comment`) so every language shares the one `--code-sintax-*` palette:
useWhen: Read-only code in docs, API examples or configuration previews that readers copy from.
The same snippet in several languages, switched by tabs (one `tabs` entry per language).
Showing a change as a diff (`lineChanges`) or pointing at one line (`highlightedLine`) on the active tab.
avoidWhen: The content is build or deploy output with timestamps and log levels → use `log-view`.
It is a marketing band that pairs a claim with its code → use `code-split`, or `sticky-scroll-code` for several claims.
It is a terminal session of CLI commands on a product page → use `cli-terminal`.
You only need to copy one short value (a token, an ID) without showing a block → use `copy-button`.
related: copy-button` — the copy control CodeBlock embeds; use it alone for one-line values.
log-view` — terminal-style viewer for CI and deploy logs.
code-split` — page section built around one code sample.
scroll-area` — the scroll container the code region runs in.
bestPractices: Put the source on each tab's `code`. There is no top-level `code` prop, and a tab without a `value` or a `code` is dropped.
Set `language` on every tab. Only JavaScript/TypeScript, shell, HCL, GraphQL and Markdown are tokenised; anything else renders as flat text.
Use `default-value` for the initial tab, and `v-model` only when something outside the block must follow the selected tab.
Set `:copyable="false"` on decorative blocks, and `:bordered="false"` when the block sits inside a surface that already frames it.
Keep `animate-lines` for marketing layouts; leave it off in docs and console screens.

props.name: tabs
props.doc: Tab definitions with label, value, code, and optional language, filename, diff, or highlight metadata.

props.name: showLineNumbers
props.doc: Shows a fixed-width gutter with zero-padded line numbers before each code line.

props.name: copyAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the copy control (forwarded to CopyButton's aria-label). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy code`).

props.name: copyable
props.doc: Shows the copy control; turn it off for a decorative block nobody copies from.

props.name: animateLines
props.doc: Staggered line entrance for website layouts: each line slides from `-8px` with opacity `0 → 1`, `40ms` apart.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw the outer card border around the block. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the block flush when it sits inside a surface that already frames it. Internal dividers (tab header, filename bar) are unaffected.

events.name: copy
events.notes: Fires after the active tab code is copied to the clipboard.

slots.name: tab-icon
slots.notes: Leading mark before a tab's label in the tab strip; nothing renders when it is not filled.
